area: Edge-case catalogue for the final app (process lifecycle, open points, supplier master, data, permissions, audit, final document, notifications, time, empty start)
summary:
Sources: context/analysis/05 and 06, the BRM acceptance criteria (v1 rows r7–r52, v2 changes) and the 9 Oct decisions with the 12 Oct answers. I checked each case against the prototype code; I read the code only and ran no tests. Paths are relative to /Users/thomas/Documents/Kissflow Projects/POC/Beiersdorf/prototype.

**Already handled, with tests:**
- The scope only grows after the completeness confirmation (src/domain/rules.ts:150-171).
- A late metadata change reopens the lead's review and gives the supplier a task (src/domain/actions.ts:171-207).
- A late origin without rules flags the case and reopens RMM's review (actions.ts:174-185).
- Only a department adds a section, in Part 2 (actions.ts:215-236).
- The final release waits for RMM and every department (actions.ts:533-546).
- Completeness blocks on mandatory fields and the K5.1 waiver (src/domain/selectors.ts:111-131).
- Rule-set and template versions are pinned per case.

**The main gaps:**
1. AS-08 is missing. There is no edit or withdraw action for the person who raised an open point, and no actor check: REQ-PROC-034 says a user without responsibility cannot change a point's status.
2. Most actions check neither the phase nor the actor. Cancelling a completed case is possible, and uploads, the composition table and justifications are accepted on frozen cases. REQ-PROC-043 says such a change attempt must be refused and logged.
3. The final release re-checks nothing. A mandatory field cleared in Part 2 reaches the frozen CIQ, and a change made after the reviews completed can be released without anyone reviewing it.
4. There is no inbox (R-1) and no final-document object (R-2/AS-12). Today they are an audit line and a disabled 'PDF not generated' note.
5. There is no supplier master, contact management or DUNS/e-mail validation. Contacts are frozen at case creation, and the supplier personas are hard-coded.
6. The audit trail has holes:
   - Part 1 answers are not logged.
   - Composition rows and justifications are never logged.
   - Metadata answers have no who/when.
   - Configuration and supplier-master changes are not logged.
7. Demo risks:
   - The seed still holds 36 cases and 10 suppliers, and the stored data version (SCHEMA) is still 6, so stale browser data survives.
   - Two open tabs overwrite each other's data in localStorage.
   - Success toasts appear even when an action was refused.
   - With zero cases, the KPIs show '0 days' and '0 %'.
8. Composition row ids are reused, and a row can be deleted while an open point refers to it.
9. A Rejected RMES decision can reach the supplier's final-release request before RMM has decided anything (AS-02).
10. Section ownership claims to apply to new cases only, but it changes running cases.

items.title: Cancel in every phase (supplier-input, review, final-release); refused when completed or already cancelled
items.current: src/domain/actions.ts:577-586: no phase guard; open points are withdrawn, but review tracks keep their status (in-review or waiting-supplier). The UI hides the button on closed cases only (src/features/rmm/CaseDetail.tsx:161-165). The dialog requires a reason (src/features/rmm/CaseActions.tsx:29-75).
items.details: Expected: only RMM can cancel (decide: any RMM or only the owner), and only in supplier-input, review or final-release. The reason is mandatory (REQ-PROC-049). Cancelling ends every task: unresolved open points become withdrawn, every track becomes inactive (no queue entry, no 'waiting' status) and the supplier's fill-in or release task is removed. The supplier gets one neutral 'request withdrawn' mail without the reason. The audit names the ended tasks, and a 'cancellation' confirmation is stored. cancelCase on a completed or cancelled case returns the state unchanged with a toast. Test, unit: in each of the 3 phases, after cancel supplierTasks() is empty, reviewQueue(dept) has no entry, every open point is closed/withdrawn and the confirmation exists; cancelling a completed case and cancelling twice are both refused. Test, E2E: RMM cancels a case in review; the supplier sees the 'withdrawn' banner and no tasks; the department's 'My reviews' list is empty.

items.title: Reactivate: back to the phase before the cancellation, inside the 12-month window, with consistent task state
items.current: src/domain/actions.ts:588-596 restores the phase but has no window guard (the UI checks it: CaseDetail.tsx:155, CaseActions.tsx:12-16). Tracks left in 'waiting-supplier' by cancelCase stay that way, so waitingOn() (src/domain/selectors.ts:49-57) reports 'supplier' with nothing open. Withdrawn points stay closed (CaseActions.tsx:106). src/store/store.tsx:159 always toasts 'reactivated', even when nothing happened.
items.details: Expected: reactivation is allowed only for a cancelled case within 365 days, enforced in the domain. The case returns to its previous phase. A waiting-supplier track with no unresolved point goes back to in-review. Withdrawn points stay closed and reviewers re-raise if needed. If the case due date has passed, the dialog asks for a new due date. The supplier gets a 'request reopened' mail and its task again. Audit entry. The toast reflects the domain result. Test, unit: cancel a review case that has a waiting-supplier track, then reactivate: no track is waiting-supplier without an open point, and waitingOn is 'bdf'. Reactivation at day 366 is refused. Reactivating a case that was never cancelled is refused with no success toast. Test, E2E: cancel and reactivate once per phase and check the stepper and the supplier task list.

items.title: Phase × action guard matrix; change attempts on a frozen CIQ refused and logged (REQ-PROC-043)
items.current: src/domain/actions.ts:250-252 (setComponents), 254-261 (setJustification) and 263-279 (uploadDocument) have no isClosed check. setAnswer silently ignores the call (240). raiseOpenPoint 388-413, supplierRespond 415-437, reviewResponse 439-462 and reopenReview 550-555 have no phase or status guards. Only the UI hides the controls (e.g. src/features/supplier/SupplierCase.tsx:107-118, Questionnaire locked).
items.details:
Expected: every domain action checks its allowed phases and object state and otherwise returns the state unchanged with an explaining toast.
- Supplier-data writes (answers, components, justifications, uploads, metadata): supplier-input, review and final-release only. On completed or cancelled cases they are refused, with an audit event 'Change attempt refused (CIQ frozen)'.
- raiseOpenPoint: review only, and only for the raiser's own active track.
- supplierRespond: only on status 'open'.
- reviewResponse: only on 'in-progress'.
- reopenReview: review or final-release only, with a mandatory reason.
- completeReview and finalRelease: already guarded; keep.
Test, unit: one table-driven test (phases × actions) asserting the case is deep-equal before and after, plus a toast, plus the frozen-attempt audit where it applies.

items.title: RMES 'Rejected' by Safety or Regulatory (AS-02): internal; RMM decides between cancel and continue before the release request
items.current: src/domain/actions.ts:499-508 (a reason is mandatory for a rejection; all criteria need results); src/features/rmm/attention.ts:47-54 (an RMM attention item); actions.ts:533-546 sends the final-release request automatically once every track is completed, even when RMM completed before the rejection.
items.details: Expected: a Rejected decision reopens a completed RMM review (system, audited). RMM's completion on a case with a Rejected decision requires an explicit choice, (a) 'Continue to final release, agreed with <dept>' with a note, or (b) 'Cancel case' with a reason. The supplier never sees the decision in the portal, mails or the final document. The decision can be changed only until that department completes. Test, unit: REG rejects after RMM completed, so the RMM track is reopened and the phase stays review; completeReview('RMM') without the continue note is refused; with it, the case reaches final-release. Test, E2E leak scan: no 'Rejected' or 'Approved' text on any supplier screen or in any supplier mail.

items.details: Expected: in Part 2, clearing a mandatory visible field is allowed only with a written justification (the REQ-PROC-012 rule, minimum length, no trivial strings). Without one, the field shows an inline error and the change is not stored. The lead reviewer of that section gets the change notice (REQ-PROC-031). finalRelease re-checks the blockers (EC-LC-10). Test, unit: setAnswer(null) on a mandatory field in review without a justification is refused; with a justification it is stored and audited. items.title: Supplier changes data or uploads after the owning review completed, or while the release request is pending
items.current: src/domain/actions.ts:243-245: setAnswer in review or final-release only writes an audit line. Nothing goes to the reviewer, nothing marks the change, nothing reopens, so the supplier can change and release at once. Upload (263-279), components (250-252) and justifications (254-261) are not even audited.
items.details:
Recommended default (decision for Thomas, since AS-03 leaves reopen-or-confirm open):
- A change in a section whose lead track is completed marks the section 'Changed since your completion', with old → new, name and time. It sends an inbox mail to that reviewer and the RMM owner. The reviewer can reopen.
- Any change or upload during final-release withdraws the release request: the case goes back to review, the affected lead gets 'Confirm no impact or reopen', and the supplier is told the release request was withdrawn (E-P-50).
- The release dialog lists every change made since the completeness confirmation (E-P-67).
Test, unit: setAnswer during final-release returns the case to review and gives the lead track a confirm-or-reopen state; an upload after the lead completed creates the marker and one mail.

items.title: Duplicate case, or a case created with missing or invalid data
items.current: src/features/rmm/NewCase.tsx:57-66 checks mandatory fields and a future due date in the UI only. src/domain/actions.ts:69-124 createCase has no validation and no duplicate check, and a missing supplier gives the audit text '(undefined)' (line 120).
items.details: Expected: the domain refuses a case without supplier, an active contact, trade name, INCI, material number, at least one market or a future due date (REQ-PROC-001). It also refuses contacts that do not belong to the supplier or are inactive. A warning appears when an open or recently completed case exists for the same supplier and material number, or the same normalised trade name (E-P-01). Continuing then needs a justification, which is audited. Test, unit: createCase with each missing field is refused; a duplicate material number returns a warning flag. Test, E2E: create the same material twice and see the warning.

Owner reassignment moves RMM's review track. This is a demo safety net: a typo at creation otherwise forces a cancel. items.title: Double submits, and success toasts after a refused action

The store shows a success toast only when the domain changed the state; otherwise it shows the domain's refusal toast alone. Repeating confirm, complete, release or cancel is a no-op with an info toast (E-D-73). items.title: Department reopens its completed review (and the release request is withdrawn)
items.current: src/domain/actions.ts:550-555: no reason check, no phase or actor guard; final-release → review (553). UI: src/features/review/CompletePanel.tsx asks for a reason, but only for non-closed cases.
items.details: Expected: only the track's own department (RMM for its lane) can reopen, in review or final-release only, with a mandatory reason. In final-release the supplier's release task disappears and the supplier gets one mail saying the release request was withdrawn. The release request is sent again exactly once when all tracks have completed (REQ-PROC-040). Test, unit: reopenReview with an empty reason, on a completed case, or by another department is refused; after reopen and re-complete, the audit shows exactly two release-request notifications in total.

items.title: AS-08: the raiser edits its open point (question, justification, due date, reference)
items.current: missing: no edit action in src/domain/actions.ts; src/features/review/OpenPointsPanel.tsx:135 offers no action while a point is 'open'; the Message action union in src/domain/types.ts:222 has no 'edited'.
items.details: Expected: only the raiser can edit, while the point is open or in-progress. The raiser is createdBy; for system-raised additional-part points it is responsibleId. An edit appends a thread entry 'Question changed' that keeps the old text. The supplier sees the current question with 'changed on <date>'. One inbox mail goes to the supplier contacts, and the edit is audited. A changed due date resets the overdue state. Closed points cannot be edited. In Kissflow this edit must update the portal twin (AS-08 API call). Test, unit: edit by a non-raiser is refused; edit on a closed point is refused; the thread keeps both texts; one mail per active contact. Test, E2E: REG edits the question; the supplier drawer shows the new text and 'changed'.

items.title: AS-08: the raiser closes or withdraws its open point at any time

The supplier's task disappears, and one mail says 'closed, no action needed' without the reason. The point stays in the supplier's list as 'Closed by Beiersdorf'. The full thread is kept and goes into the final document. items.title: Point edited or closed by its raiser while the supplier is writing the answer
items.current: src/features/supplier/AnswerDrawer.tsx:156 shows the composer only while the point is 'open', from the state at render time. src/domain/actions.ts:415-437 supplierRespond accepts any status and has no question-version check.

On send, a closed or withdrawn point refuses the answer with 'Beiersdorf closed this question on <date>', and the typed text and file stay in the drawer to copy. An edited point shows 'The question changed, please review' with the new text, and the supplier sends again. In Kissflow the portal write must check the same version. Test, unit: supplierRespond with a stale version or on a closed point returns the state unchanged with a toast. Test, E2E (sequential personas): the supplier opens the drawer and types; then REG withdraws the point; the supplier sends and the refusal message appears with the text kept.

items.title: Only the raiser or responsible reviewer decides on, edits or closes a point (REQ-PROC-034)

items.title: Repeated clarification loop, cannot-provide, and 'not accepted' (deadlock exit)

items.title: Stable composition row ids; deleting a row that an open point refers to

Lines 124-128 allow removing any row while the section is not locked, including in Part 2, even when an open point has ref.rowId on it. src/domain/actions.ts:250-252 replaces the whole array and writes no audit.

Row changes are stored per row (add, update, remove) with who and when, and audited in Part 2 (REQ-PROC-031). items.title: R-1: an inbox per person; one mail per open-point raise, answer, edit and close; never internal content
items.current: missing: no mail model. src/features/admin/EmailPreviews.tsx:11-25 is a static table with 'no e-mail is sent'. The audit writes 'Notified supplier' only at createCase (src/domain/actions.ts:122) and raiseOpenPoint (410).
items.details:
Expected: an inbox for every user (internal and supplier).
- Raise, edit, return, accept, not-accepted and withdraw: one mail to each active assigned supplier contact of the case.
- A supplier answer or cannot-provide: one mail to the raiser (responsibleId for system points); decide whether the RMM owner gets a copy.
- Every mail names the material, the case ID, the item reference and a deep link. It never contains internal reasons, finding text, RMES results or decisions, internal notes or department statuses.
- Each mail is logged on the case (REQ-CTL-010). Deactivated contacts get nothing, and events are idempotent (one mail per event per recipient).
Test, unit: a mail builder test per event (recipients, count) plus a leak scan of supplier mail bodies against the case's internal strings. Test, E2E: after each action, the expected inbox shows the mail and the deep link opens the right item.

items.title: Lifecycle mails: invitation, the single final-release request, final document to RMM, cancellation notice, release request withdrawn
items.current: Audit text only: src/domain/actions.ts:122 (invitation), 538-544 ('Exactly one notification…'), 560 (PDF e-mailed). No cancellation notice.
items.details: Expected: the invitation goes to all invited contacts at creation. Exactly ONE release-request mail goes out after the last track completes, even with 6 tracks, and none per individual completion (REQ-PROC-040). A final-document mail with a link goes to the RMM owner at release (REQ-PROC-046). A neutral 'request withdrawn' mail goes out on cancel, and a 'release request withdrawn' mail on reopen. Test, unit: completing 6 tracks in any order gives exactly one supplier release mail; a reopen and re-complete gives a second one, not more.

items.title: Due dates, overdue and reminders
items.current: Case due date must be in the future in the UI only (src/features/rmm/NewCase.tsx:65). Open-point due date must be today or later (src/features/review/AskModals.tsx:48). A returned point gets at least 7 more days (src/domain/actions.ts:450-452); system additional parts get 14 days (201). The final-release task inherits the case due date (src/domain/selectors.ts:220), so it can be born overdue. Overdue shows in CaseDetail.tsx:57,90-91, OpenPointsPanel.tsx:110 and the supplier DueText. Reminders are configuration only (src/domain/seed.ts:398-404) and never run. Due dates are stored at 16:00Z or 17:00Z.
items.details: Expected: the domain validates due dates (not in the past). The final-release task gets its own due date (request + N days, reminder rem-5). The raiser can change a point's due date through the AS-08 edit, and RMM can change the case due date (REQ-ADR-001: it stays flexible); both are audited and mailed. Overdue counts agree between the dashboard, the case and the supplier view. Reminders show as derived, idempotent inbox entries once a task passes its threshold (one per threshold), with an escalation copy to the RMM owner. A due date means the end of the user's local day. Test, unit (actions and isOverdue take 'at'): with at = due + 1 day the point is overdue everywhere; the release task due date is request + N; the reminder entry count stays at one after repeated evaluation.

items.title: Supplier master: view suppliers and add a new supplier with validation

proposals:
TEST PLAN (the overnight gate: typecheck, vitest, build, build:portal, harness-portal, plus a new prototype harness)

1. Fixtures. buildSeed() becomes the empty demo start (EC-SM-01). Move the SPECS replay (src/domain/seed.ts:111-383) into a test-only fixture module, e.g. src/domain/fixtures.ts with buildRichFixture(). The existing tests (seed.test.ts, attention.test.ts, lib.test.ts) and the portal fixtures (scripts/portal-fixtures.ts) then keep a rich dataset. Add a small scenario builder for new tests, for example:
   `sc().supplier('s1').create({markets:['EU','UK']}).answerAllMetadata({SF01:['vegetable']}).fillMandatory().confirm().raise('REG',{field:'FLD-K1-002'}).answer('u-sup-2').accept().completeAll().release()`
   It uses the pure actions with explicit 'at' timestamps, so due-date and reminder tests are deterministic.

2. Invariants. Add a pure checkInvariants(state) in src/domain and call it after every step of every scenario test. Optionally also run it in dev builds and log any violation with console.error, so the E2E harness fails on it.
   - final-release ⇒ every track completed and no unresolved open point;
   - completed ⇒ exactly one finalDocument and one final-release confirmation;
   - cancelled ⇒ supplierTasks empty, no active track, no unresolved point;
   - no completed track with an unresolved point of its own department;
   - no unresolved point on an N.A. section;
   - every open point's department has a track;
   - every audit event has a by and an ISO at;
   - supplier-facing mails contain no internal marker strings;
   - deactivated contacts have no task, inbox entry or action after deactivation;
   - every open case has at least one active contact.

3. Unit test files to add, all vitest and all domain-level:
   - guards.test.ts: the phase × action matrix (EC-LC-03) and the actor checks (EC-PM-03, EC-PM-05, EC-OP-04).
   - openpoints.test.ts: AS-08 edit and withdraw; the race with a stale version (EC-OP-03); the loop; row-id stability (EC-OP-06).
   - lifecycle.test.ts: cancel and reactivate in each phase; the 12-month window; a stale waiting-supplier track; release blockers; a mandatory field cleared in Part 2; a change during final-release; the RMES Rejected gate.
   - supplierMaster.test.ts: the DUNS and e-mail validators; duplicate rules; contact deactivation with open cases.
   - notify.test.ts: recipients and counts per event; exactly one release request; the leak scan.
   - finalDocument.test.ts: content, exclusions, once-only, immutability.
   - audit.test.ts: every action appends an event; the global configuration log.
   - metrics-empty.test.ts: zero-case KPIs give '—', not 0.

4. E2E harness: scripts/harness-prototype.mjs, modelled on scripts/harness-portal.mjs. Reuse its playwright-core path (harness-portal.mjs:16, borrowed from /Users/thomas/Documents/Kissflow Projects/POC/Promotion Management/app/node_modules/playwright-core). Serve the built dist on a local port. Every scenario gets a fresh browser context (empty localStorage) and switches personas through the real role switcher. Every scenario asserts no console errors, no 'NaN', 'undefined' or 'Infinity' text, and checkInvariants clean. Scenarios:
   - S0: empty start × every persona × every route, using the role-route matrix (EC-EM-01, EC-PM-06).
   - S1: the full happy path from nothing. Add a supplier, create the case, both contacts fill different sections, confirm completeness, RMM and the departments raise, answer, accept and complete, release, open the final document, check the inboxes.
   - S2: late metadata change in review (EC-LC-04).
   - S3: a department adds a section, and the supplier completes it (EC-LC-06).
   - S4: AS-08 edit and withdraw, including the race with the drawer open (EC-OP-01 to EC-OP-03).
   - S5: RMES Rejected after RMM completed (EC-LC-09).
   - S6: cancel and reactivate once per phase (EC-LC-01, EC-LC-02).
   - S7: release blocked by a mandatory field cleared in Part 2 (EC-LC-10, EC-LC-11).
   - S8: supplier-master validation and contact deactivation (EC-SM-02, EC-SM-03).
   - S9: supplier leak scan with marker strings (EC-PM-01).
   - S10: two pages in one context (EC-DT-02).
   - S11: final document immutability (EC-FD-01).
   - S12: morning check. A fresh load shows 0 cases, 1 supplier and its 2 contacts, and 'Reset demo data' returns exactly that.

DECISIONS FOR THOMAS (each with the default used in the catalogue)
- (a) Contact access. Default: every active contact of the supplier sees and acts on all its cases. Alternative: only the contacts assigned per case (REQ-CTL-001 says the supplier assigns its own tasks).
- (b) Supplier answer mails. Default: to the raiser only; the RMM owner sees the answer in the app. Alternative: also copy the RMM owner, as EmailPreviews says today.
- (c) A change during final-release. Default: it withdraws the release request and asks the lead to confirm no impact or reopen. Alternative: notify only.
- (d) Final document for the supplier. Default: no; the supplier gets a release receipt.
- (e) Who may cancel and reactivate. Default: any RMM; the case owner is shown.
- (f) Who may decide, edit or withdraw an open point. Default: the person who raised it (AS-08 wording). Alternative: anyone in the raising department.
- (g) An e-mail used by contacts of two suppliers. Default: refused.
- (h) The internal discussion. Default: Customs and Legal may post; Admin, Business owner and Auditor read only.
- (i) Correction requests. Default: the portal's CIQP Change Request is not in the final app before the release, since the supplier edits directly. After the release, a change means a new case.
- (j) RMES Rejected. Default: it reopens RMM's review, and RMM must explicitly choose 'continue' (with a note) or cancel.

NOTES FOR THE KISSFLOW BUILD (from the same edge cases)
- Concurrent edits: the portal's per-section Answers_JSON needs field-level merge or optimistic locking (EC-DT-01).
- AS-08 edits and withdrawals must update the portal twin through the integration API (EC-OP-01, EC-OP-02).
- The final document is produced by the external script on the release webhook (AS-12). It must build its text only from data that may be shown and must store a hash (EC-FD-01).
- Section ownership and template/rule-set versions must be pinned on the case record (EC-PM-07).
